Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
904 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Water levels continue to decrease. Forecast snow totals for
tonight in the Alleghenies were increased slightly.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Snow showers and freezing drizzle continue in the
  Alleghenies overnight.

- 2) Another potent area of low pressure brings precipitation
     and blustery conditions Sunday night into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Snow showers and freezing drizzle continue in
the Alleghenies overnight. 

An area of low pressure is now centered close to the NY/Quebec
border and will continue to track northeastward off toward the
Canadian Maritimes overnight. Flow locally continues to be out
of the west to southwest behind the departing low. While upslope
flow into the Alleghenies isn't at the ideal angle (WSW as
opposed to WNW to NW), the boundary layer is very moisture 
laden, with nearly saturated low-levels and low ceilings
upstream across the Ohio Valley. As a result, on and off upslope
snow showers are expected to continue through much of the night
in the Alleghenies. The forecast in terms of accumulations is a
difficult one, since there are a few complicating factors.
First, surface temperatures are very marginal, especially below
3000 ft. Currently temperatures are 32-34 at most locations
below 3000 ft, so accumulations are somewhat dependent on
snowfall rates overcoming residual heat in the ground. The loss
of daytime heating from the sun should help with the efficiency
of accumulations, but some of the precipitation will still
likely be lost to melting, especially when it's lighter in
nature. Second, model soundings suggest that there could be loss
of ice crystals at times overnight as the subsidence inversion
starts to lower and saturation is lost at temperatures colder
than -5 to -7 C. This could lead to some of the snow turning 
over to freezing drizzle at times. For now, we're expecting a 
general 1 to 3 inches of snow in the Alleghenies overnight, 
along with a light glaze of ice. Isolated slightly higher totals
could be possible above 3000 feet. Winter Weather Advisories 
remain in effect for western Grant and western Pendleton 
counties through 7 AM. Elsewhere, mostly cloudy skies are 
expected overnight, with overnight lows in the 30s to lower 40s.

Any snow showers or freezing drizzle in the Alleghenies should
come to an end shortly after daybreak tomorrow as the subsidence
inversion further lowers. Residual clouds should tend to break
up over the course of the day, leading to a fair amount of
sunshine by tomorrow afternoon. Winds will be gusty out of the
west, but temperatures will run a bit warmer, with highs in the
mid to upper 50s for most (30s/40s mountains).


KEY MESSAGE 2...Another potent area of low pressure brings precipitation
and blustery conditions Sunday night into Monday.

High pressure will keep the region dry Sunday. Temperatures will be 
near seasonable with highs middle 50s to lower 60s. 

As the high pushes further to the southeast Sunday night, a low 
pressure system will move from the middle Mississippi Valley on 
Sunday toward the eastern Great Lakes Sunday night. A trailing cold 
front will push across the region Sunday night into Monday morning.
Showers will likely accompany the front. We can't rule out a clap of 
thunder or two either given that there will be plenty of wind shear, 
despite instability being minimal to nil and the time of night for 
frontal passage. Highs cooler Sunday with highs mainly in lower to 
upper 50s.

As the front pushes through, winds will pick up substantially out of 
the northwest on Monday in its wake. Wind gusts, especially along 
the ridges out west, could approach wind advisory criteria. Areas 
along the MD/PA border will also see gusts close to criteria, but 
not very high confidence in the exact magnitude at this time. Still, 
potential for downed trees given the wet ground from the previous 
system. Otherwise, highs Monday reach the upper 40s to mid 50s 
outside of the mountains (they'll be in the 20s to 30s). Wind chills 
will be quite cold on the ridges Monday, with values in the teens at 
the highest elevations. 

Once the front moves to the east and southeast Monday afternoon, 
high pressure will become reestablished and bring dry conditions and 
seasonable temperatures to the region through the middle of the 
week.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are forecast over the next several 
days, although there could be a brief period later tonight with 
some MVFR ceilings. Winds will lose some of their gustiness 
tonight, but remain around 10 kt. Winds pick up again Saturday 
with daytime mixing with gusts to around 20-25 kt expected. 
Winds become lighter on Sunday as high pressure builds traverses
the area, but turn from a southerly direction. Showers are 
expected Sunday night.

Winds out of the WNW Monday afternoon at around 15 to 25 knots, 
gusting up to 35 to 40 knots at times in the wake of a powerful cold 
front. Flight category should return to VFR by Monday morning and 
remain that way through at least the middle of the week.

&&

.MARINE...
All Gale Warnings have been dropped as winds continue to
diminish. However, SCA conditions will continue through
Saturday with gusts up to 25 kt expected. 

An area of low pressure will slide by to our northwest Sunday into 
Monday. Gale-force winds are possible Monday in the wake of the cold 
front associated with this system. Winds will rapidly taper off 
Monday night into Tuesday, with any marine headlines likely dropping 
overnight Monday. Light and variable winds prevail Tuesday and 
Wednesday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies continue to decrease this evening. This
evening's tide cycle is expected to be the final one with
coastal flooding issues as anomalies continue to drop rapidly 
through the day Saturday.

&&
